_comment: Build-loop AND digest targets. The scripts know nothing about any
particular codebase or journey; a target profile tells them where to work,
what to read, what to stage and how to verify. Adding a target is a data
edit, not a script change.
A run picks its target from, in order: an explicit --target flag, the
backlog's top-level "target" field, .digest-meta.json's "target", then the
default below. See target-profile.sh.
verify.* are npm script names run in the target repo. Omit one to skip that
rung of the ladder.
sources[] drives prepare-digest.sh. Each entry needs an id and a type; what
else it needs depends on the type:
confluence — ref is the page id. Fetched via tools/confluence/page.sh and
cached as <id>.page.json plus <id>.body.html (body.view, not
body.storage, which is empty on some pages).
canvas     — ref is a path relative to the target repo. Copied verbatim.
code       — ref is a path inside the repo; pinned to the base sha at
prepare time and read live by the extractor, not cached.
An entry marked "pending": true keeps its real type but is neither fetched
nor given an extract placeholder. It is seeded into the spec's sources[]
with status "pending", so a later hand-filled extract has somewhere to
belong — that is how figma arrived on the live-animals run.
backlogTail drives the fixed tail backlog-generate.sh appends after the
per-page increments. Both keys are optional; omit them and the tail is
empty, which is what a greenfield set wants.
